One concrete resource regression found: the periodic real-space cache can retain gigabytes per degree for supported large 3D shell limits. The owner agreed to cap it at 1,024 samples, evaluating subsequent samples without storage.

No other concrete defects found in:

  • Field harmonic table keys, scaling, sparse dispatch or Hessian recurrences.
  • Periodic cache sequencing, preserved small-split safeguards or planar derivative truncation.
  • S-matrix contraction certification, dense fallback, reflection ownership or adjoint multiplication order.
  • Interaction with the single-column GMRES wrapper.

I reviewed source only. No builds, tests or timings run. The cache cap remains to be inspected after the measurement freeze.

items.html:
One concrete issue: Krylov::new eagerly allocates its quadratic Hessenberg buffer before checking whether a column already meets tolerance. Zero or tiny RHS columns with a large supported restart now incur potentially large allocations; main returned immediately. Sent the owner a recommendation to allocate in start().

Otherwise, independent restart/iteration limits, early-finishing columns, true-residual checks, column mapping and deterministic reduction order are preserved.

Coverage gap: the coupled-physics batch tests mostly use weak, low-order spheres. I recommended a compact, higher-order cluster with enough iterations to cross several short restarts, checked against dense forward and adjoint results. Synthetic tests already cover mixed scales, zeros, differing completion times and independent iteration budgets.

Read-only review; no builds or timings run.

  • Field sequences preserve scaling and per-centre/wavenumber limits.
  • Harmonic cache keys remain valid.

One minor behavior change: invalid translation arguments can now produce AMOS error wording rather than the previous radial-validation wording. They remain rejected.
